name: Ahaziah of Israel
charge: Inquiring of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron
summary: Ahab's son fell through a lattice in Samaria and sent messengers to ask Baal-zebub whether he would recover. Elijah met them on the road: is it not because there is not a God in Israel that ye go to inquire of Baal-zebub? Two captains of fifty sent to arrest the prophet were consumed by fire.
offense: After falling through a lattice and becoming sick, Ahaziah sent to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron. Elijah intercepted the messengers with the question whether there was no God in Israel that the king sought this answer elsewhere (2 Kings 1:2-4). The inquiry exposed whom he trusted when his own life became uncertain. Recognising Elijah from the messengers' description, Ahaziah sent soldiers to summon him. Two captains addressed the man of God with the king's demand, and fire consumed their companies (2 Kings 1:9-12). Royal force did not give the king command over the word already pronounced against him.
judgment: The third captain knelt and pleaded that his life and his men's lives be precious. The angel told Elijah to go with him and not fear (2 Kings 1:13-15). The change from command to humble petition distinguished this company from those before it. Before Ahaziah, Elijah repeated the sentence: because he had sent to Ekron, he would not come down from his bed but would die. He died according to the word, and Jehoram succeeded him because he had no son (2 Kings 1:16-17). Bringing the prophet before the throne had not brought the judgment under the throne's control.

entries.commentary: Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High. -

Ahaziah falls down through a lattice in his upper chamber and is sick, and sends messengers to inquire of Beelzebub, the god of Ekron, the lord of the flies, whether he shall recover. He turns to an idol rather than to the Most High for his answer. The angel of the Lord sends Elijah the Tishbite to meet the messengers and ask whether it is because there is no God in Israel that they go to inquire of Beelzebub. The word of the Lord is that Ahaziah shall not come down from his bed but shall surely die. When the messengers describe the hairy man girt with a girdle of leather who met them, the king knows it is Elijah. Ahaziah should have known the history that would have kept him from trusting the god of Ekron. -

The king sends a captain of fifty with his fifty to Elijah, who sits on the top of a hill, and the captain commands the man of God to come down. Elijah answers that if he is a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume him and his fifty, and it does. A second captain of fifty is sent and speaks the same way, and fire from heaven consumes him and his fifty as well. The third captain goes up, falls on his knees, and pleads that his life and the lives of his fifty be precious in Elijah's sight. The angel of the Lord tells Elijah to go down with the third captain and not to fear him. Elijah delivers to the king the same word, that because he sent to inquire of Beelzebub as though there were no God in Israel, he shall surely die.

Ahaziah dies according to the word of the Lord that Elijah had spoken, and Jehoram reigns in his stead because Ahaziah had no son. The rest of the acts of Ahaziah are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

Ye shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy; this word went to all the congregation of the children of Israel. Fear every man his mother and his father goes back to the commandment, honour thy father and thy mother. Honour can be kept even at a distance: show respect, and do nothing that would bring shame on your mother. But there is a balance; if she asks for what is against the commandments of the Most High, the commandments come first. Keep my sabbaths: the feast days are Sabbaths also. The Passover, the first and last days of the feast of Tabernacles, the day of atonement, and the memorial of blowing of trumpets are all Sabbaths; no servile work, no buying and selling, though cooking is permitted on the feast days.
Turn not unto idols, nor make molten gods; this is the commandment against making any graven image.

The peace offering was eaten the same day it was offered or on the morrow; whatever remained to the third day was burnt. Eaten on the third day it is abominable, and the eater bears his iniquity, for he has profaned the hallowed thing of the Lord.

The corners of the field, the gleanings of the harvest, and the leavings of the vineyard belonged to the poor and the stranger. The Most High is teaching, do not be selfish; love thy neighbour as thyself and look out for the poor of your people. He that provides not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, has denied the faith. Those of his own house are his wife and children; his own is his nation. Care for your people. Charge them that are rich that they be not highminded, but ready to distribute, willing to communicate. Most of us today have no fields or vineyards, but some have good jobs and blessed incomes; you cannot take it with you, so give of your substance. The scriptures also say no good can come to him that gives no alms.

Dealing falsely is any dishonesty: skewing the truth to get your way, or cheating. Be honest. Have an honest job so you do not steal; run an honest business so you do not cheat people with foul practices, selling goods you know will fail or charging a customer for repairs he does not need. That honesty is owed even to the other nations.

Do not swear by His name falsely. Saying I swear to God over a lie profanes the name of the Most High. Christ said swear not at all, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by thy head; let your communication be yea, yea and nay, nay. The only reason a man swears is that he has lied before and no one believes him; in your repentance take swearing out of your speech, and do not put oaths on your own head or your family either.

The wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning: when a man works for you, pay him that same day. Holding back the wage is defrauding thy neighbour, so businesses in Israel should pay their people the way the scriptures say. If both parties agree beforehand to payment the next day, that agreement is between you, the Lord, and that man; the scripture states the standard.

Curse not the deaf, put no stumblingblock before the blind, but fear thy God. Do no unrighteousness in judgment; respect not the person of the poor nor honour the person of the mighty. The courts of this land do the opposite: our people receive far harsher sentences than others for the same crime with the same priors, sometimes before the very same judge.

A talebearer revealeth secrets, but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter. What a brother or sister tells you in confidence is not yours to spread; carrying it to the next person is talebearing, and it happens even in this truth. Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: much strife and contention comes from messy people. Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel.

Hate not thy brother in thine heart; rebuke thy neighbour and suffer not sin upon him. If you love your brother or sister you correct them when they are going off into sin; that is real love. Love thy neighbour as thyself: thy neighbour is the children of thy people. Get that right, against the teaching that makes the neighbour everybody.
Keep the statutes: no gendering cattle with a diverse kind, no sowing the field with mingled seed, and no garment mingled of linen and woollen; that is the law against mixed fabrics.

The bondmaid betrothed to an husband and not redeemed was scourged, not put to death, because she was not free; the man brought a ram for a trespass offering, and the priest made atonement, and the sin was forgiven him.

Fruit of a newly planted tree was counted as uncircumcised for three years and not eaten; in the fourth year all the fruit was holy to praise the Lord withal; only in the fifth year could the fruit be eaten, that it might yield its increase.

Eat nothing with the blood: cook the blood out of the meat. No rare or bloody meat, none of the raw-meat customs of the other nations. Use no enchantments nor observe times; that goes into the horoscopes, astrology, and the rest of that nonsense. Leave it alone.

Round not the corners of your head, meaning do not bald your head; mar not the corners of thy beard, meaning do not shave off the beard. This is written to all the children of Israel, not to the priests only.

No cuttings in the flesh for the dead, nor any marks printed upon you: that is the tattoo. The RIP tattoo for a dead family member is both a cutting in the flesh for the dead and a mark printed upon you. If you came into this truth already carrying tattoos, repent, ask the Most High for forgiveness, and get no more. Ear and nose piercings are not forbidden by this verse; the cutting forbidden here is the cutting in the flesh for the dead.

Prostituting your daughter to cause her to be a whore takes several forms: letting her dress immodestly, letting a little girl wear makeup and grown attire, and letting her have a boyfriend. There are no boyfriends and girlfriends in the scriptures. The father waketh for the daughter: his charge is to watch over her, know her clothes, her phone, her friends and their parents, and keep her under supervision, lest she pass away the flower of her age, which is her virginity being taken. Keeping a sure watch over her is not being too hard on her; it is the commandment, lest she make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies. Many daughters go the way of the mother, as the proverb says, as is the mother, so is her daughter; but Israel is teaching the sisters self-respect again, with the scriptures on modest apparel and on not wearing that which pertaineth to a man. When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law.

Keep my sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards to be defiled by them. Rise up before the hoary head and honour the face of the old man: show respect unto your elders.

Vex not the stranger that sojourns with thee in the land; he shall be as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. The stranger of this law is an Israelite of another tribe sojourning outside the allotment of his own tribe: a man of Judah dwelling in the land of Benjamin is a stranger to that land, because that was not the allotment the Most High gave him. When your brother the stranger falls into decay, relieve him and let him sojourn with you; give him work to deliver him out of his low state until he can stand again. The bondmen laws show the contrast in how the word stranger is used. The bondmen and bondmaids were to be of the heathen round about, and in that context the children of the strangers sojourning among you are the heathen, a possession and an inheritance; but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule with rigour. Then the sojourner or stranger that waxeth rich by thee returns to the Israelite stranger, for the bondservant of the heathen did not wax rich.

Just balances, just weights, a just ephah and a just hin. Falsifying the balance is rigging the scale so that one pound weighs out as two and the buyer pays double; our people were doing that wickedness, and the Most High requires honest measure. Therefore observe all my statutes and all my judgments and do them: the Lord which brought Israel out of the land of Egypt requires it.
The Most High told Isaiah to take a great roll and write in it with a man's pen concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz, meaning quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil.

Isaiah took faithful witnesses to record, Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah, then went to the prophetess, who conceived and bare a son. The Most High said to call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz, for before the child shall have knowledge to cry, "My father, and my mother," the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria. This ties to [Isaiah 7:16](/bible/isaiah/7#v16), "before the child shall know to refuse evil and choose the good"; both point to the fall of the lands of Rezin and Pekah.

Because the people refuse the waters of Shiloah that go softly and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah's son, the Most High brings upon them the waters of the river strong and many, the king of Assyria and all his glory, rising over all his channels and banks. He shall pass through Judah and overflow, reaching even to the neck, and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of the land, O Immanuel, which means God with us.

"Associate yourselves, O ye people, and ye shall be broken in pieces." Though the far countries gird themselves, they shall be broken; take counsel together and it shall come to nought, speak the word and it shall not stand, for God is with us. If the counsel is from man it will fall, but if it is from the Most High it cannot be overthrown, and men would only end up fighting against God. -

The Most High spoke with a strong hand, instructing Isaiah not to walk in the way of this people, and not to say "a confederacy" to all them to whom this people says a confederacy, nor to fear their fear. "Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread."

He shall be for a sanctuary, but also a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, and a gin and snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. He is a sanctuary for his people, a little sanctuary in the places where they are scattered, but a stone of stumbling to those who reject him. The word became a snare upon the leadership because the understanding is given precept upon precept, in another tongue, so that those without it stumble and fall. -
Many among them shall stumble, fall, be broken, snared, and taken.

"Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples." Knowing the law is knowing what the mark truly is, instead of thinking of a microchip and being snared and taken by every wind, like the trees moved with the wind.

"I will wait upon the LORD, that hideth his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him." Behold, Isaiah and the children the Most High gave him are for signs and wonders in Israel, from the Lord of hosts which dwelleth in mount Zion.

When they say to seek unto them that have familiar spirits, and wizards that peep and mutter, the answer is: should not a people seek unto their God? For the living to the dead? "To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them." Christians say Jesus is the word and go to [John 17:17](/bible/john/17#v17), "thy word is truth," but the word spoken of is the law; no law means no light, which is why there is no light in christianity. -

They shall pass through it hardly bestead and hungry, fret themselves, and curse their king and their God, looking upward and to the earth. They shall behold trouble and darkness, dimness of anguish, and be driven to darkness.

verses.text: And Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber that was in Samaria, and was sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease.

But the angel of the Lord said to Elijah the Tishbite, Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say unto them, Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron?
Now therefore thus saith the Lord, Thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die. And Elijah departed.

And they said unto him, There came a man up to meet us, and said unto us, Go, turn again unto the king that sent you, and say unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that thou sendest to enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron? therefore thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.
Then the king sent unto him a captain of fifty with his fifty. And he went up to him: and, behold, he sat on the top of an hill. And he spake unto him, Thou man of God, the king hath said, Come down.

And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, If I be a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
Again also he sent unto him another captain of fifty with his fifty. And he answered and said unto him, O man of God, thus hath the king said, Come down quickly.

And Elijah answered and said unto them, If I be a man of God, let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And the fire of God came down from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
And the angel of the Lord said unto Elijah, Go down with him: be not afraid of him. And he arose, and went down with him unto the king.

And he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Forasmuch as thou hast sent messengers to enquire of Baal–zebub the god of Ekron, is it not because there is no God in Israel to enquire of his word? therefore thou shalt not come down off that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.
So he died according to the word of the Lord which Elijah had spoken. And Jehoram reigned in his stead in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah; because he had no son.
Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards, to be defiled by them: I am the Lord your God.
And when they shall say unto you, Seek unto them that have familiar spirits, and unto wizards that peep, and that mutter: should not a people seek unto their God? for the living to the dead?

lawsResolved.text: Divination, soothsaying, and the use of mediums, spiritists and occultists are forbidden practices.
We are not to listen to diviners, enchanters, mediums or sorcerers.
Those in government are not to consult mediums or spiritists for guidance but are to inquire of the LORD.
A man or a woman with a familiar spirit or who is a wizard shall be put to death.
